text: This service holds no timer entity. The plan clock is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow of rwb-case, projected behind the case timers operation, and rwb-treatment holds only the plan facts the clock is built from (first_due_date, installments, installment_amount, installments_paid, installment_shortfall), which it publishes on rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1; the treatment state follows the case and payment signals and this service never writes a case state, a timer row or a TimerDue event.
why: The context pack gives S2 one owned table (treatment) and no job, the legacy timer table and its unique plan index would create a second clock, and RWB-P3-E2004-CON retires TimerScheduler, JOB-05 and TimerDue and declares the timer row a projection of rwb-case.

text: A case holds at most one treatment in state RUNNING at a time, enforced by the partial unique index ux_treatment_running_plan on treatment(case_id) where state = 'RUNNING'; the request idempotency is carried by the Idempotency-Key header and an inbox row and the event idempotency by the CloudEvents id, so no idempotency column is added to the treatment table. Feature switch rwb.treatment.plan-model is off outside production until the migration is applied.
why: The legacy guard was a unique index on the timer table for one due date, the timer is gone, and no source restates the guard on the treatment row; TSD S2 publishes no idempotency column and the platform library owns the dedupe table.
